sessions.title: VLE and flash calculations
sessions.claim: Bubble/dew boundaries and flash are different questions.
sessions.outcome: Predict a two-phase state, solve it, then check both component balances.
sessions.deliverable: In Lab 01, save one ideal two-phase baseline and one changed pressure at the same T and z. Predict the change, report phase amounts and check one component balance by hand.
sessions.preparation: Read the P-x-y example and bring a phase prediction at 110 kPa. Prepare the three short questions on page 3.
sessions.guidingQuestion: How does pressure change the phase split at fixed temperature?
sessions.optionalPractice: Choose one extension: compare liquid activity models, examine zero versus nonzero virial coefficients in Lab 09, or add the energy balance in Lab 07.

sessions.title: Experimental VLE, consistency and fitting
sessions.claim: A small fitting error does not validate the observations.
sessions.outcome: Separate vapor-pressure inputs, consistency evidence and fitted-model error.
sessions.deliverable: Complete worksheet pages 1–4: phase and material-balance checks, activity and Antoine calculations, the Lab 08 baseline and independent property check, two model fits, interpretation, and your own Q1–Q6 review-test attempt. Submit it in the attendance form, then view the worked solutions and optionally submit corrections. Keep the baseline and both model exports. These activities, the break, exit ticket and feedback are included in the 180-minute lesson; there is no additional compulsory follow-up.
sessions.preparation: This is optional background. Start with the lesson instructions; no prior knowledge of activity coefficients or real dataset is required.
sessions.guidingQuestion: Does a small fitting error mean the data and model are trustworthy?
sessions.optionalPractice: Choose one extension: the published case study in Lab 02, a fixed held-out comparison, bootstrap fit spread, or your own sourced VLE data. Exact synthetic bootstrap spread does not quantify real measurement uncertainty. Controlled consistency tests in Lab 03 are core work in Session 3.
sessions.clarificationNote: Session 3 is a 180-minute independent holiday lesson. Its first 15 minutes review Week 2; consistency tests in Lab 03 then come before stability and LLE in Lab 04. Use the Lab 08 guide for units, CSV, saved studies and model evidence. No repeat Session 2 attendance submission is required.

sessions.title: Thermodynamic consistency, liquid stability and LLE
sessions.claim: A good model fit is not a consistency test, and an equilibrium root is not proof of stability.
sessions.outcome: Use hand calculations and controlled Lab 03 comparisons to interpret consistency evidence, then distinguish stable, metastable and unstable homogeneous feeds from the final liquid equilibrium.
sessions.deliverable: Complete worksheet sections A–I. Retain a VLE retrieval calculation; Gibbs–Duhem path assumptions; hand area and local-residual calculations; predictions and a Lab 03 comparison including 41 versus 161 points; one clean-reference model fit; an explanation of diagnostic disagreement; a Lab 04 comparison of stable, metastable and unstable homogeneous feeds with their final equilibria; an independent phase-amount balance; and your own unseen-case review attempt with corrections. Finish the existing exit ticket and feedback. These are the required outputs in the planned 180-minute route; there is no additional compulsory follow-up.
sessions.preparation: Open the study guide, narrated lesson, worksheet and Lab guide. Follow the main activity checkpoints, attempt each problem before its solution, and continue when the required output is ready. The video and slides are alternative presentations of the same lesson. Suggested study times are planning estimates, not minimum waiting periods or measured student completion times. No prior compulsory reading is needed.
sessions.guidingQuestion: What evidence supports consistent VLE data, and what additional evidence supports a stable liquid split?
sessions.optionalPractice: After completing the core lesson, optional extensions include NRTL tie-line fitting in Lab 05, paired bootstrap from independent replicates, or feasible three-phase amounts in Lab 06. A paper exercise connects tangent intercepts to partial molar properties in the appendix. These are not required in the 180-minute lesson.
sessions.completionNote: At minutes 155–170, attempt the unseen-case review in section H before checking the worked solutions; retain the first attempt and corrections. At 170–180, use the existing Session 3 exit form: answer its LLE concept question and include consistency-test evidence. In the existing feedback text, report the minutes you actually spent and whether the pace felt too fast, suitable or too slow. Submit once, wait for the receipt and save your work. The anonymous form does not identify attendance.
sessions.assessmentSummary: Complete A1–A3 and B1–B3 on worksheet page 1: VLE retrieval, the Gibbs–Duhem slope relationship, path assumptions and missing information. Complete the area and local-residual calculations C1–C6 on page 2. On page 3, follow the Lab 03 demonstration and complete D1–D5 and E1–E2: predict before canceling and localized changes, compare the localized case at 41 and 161 points, run one clean 41-point fit, and annotate a residual plot with a supported interpretation. Pages 4–5, F1–F3 and G1–G4, compare A = 3 feeds z = 0.02, 0.12 and 0.50, their homogeneous stability and final equilibrium; independently check the balances at z = 0.12 and 0.50 and explain the tangent and energy evidence. Attempt H1–H4 on page 6 before the solutions, then complete I using the existing anonymous exit ticket and feedback. The planned 180 minutes include viewing, work, review and the 10-minute break; there is no additional compulsory follow-up.
sessions.assessmentEvidence: Record each method, its inputs, result and applicability. Retain the hand area and local-residual calculations, predictions, Lab 03 baseline and controlled changes including resolution, and the homogeneous-feed versus equilibrium comparison in Lab 04. Include an independent component balance, a supported conclusion and limitation, and the unseen-case first attempt plus corrections. Synthetic diagnostic outcomes do not certify real data or predictive validity.
schedule: A · Review VLE and model evidence
Open the lesson and worksheet p. 1, A1–A3. Output: definitions, one checked activity calculation and a fit-versus-consistency statement.
B · Gibbs–Duhem and the experimental path

Worksheet p. 2, C1–C6; Lab guide p. 1. Output: signed areas, the worked local example, your independent local residual and a numerical caveat.

Lab 03; worksheet p. 3, D1–D5 and E1–E2; guide pp. 2–3. Output: two predictions, clean/canceling/localized comparison, localized 41-versus-161-point check, one clean 41-point fit and an annotated plot with a claim and limitation.
Save your work and take a 10-minute break.
F–G · Homogeneous stability and final LLE
Lab 04; worksheet pp. 4–5, F1–F3 and G1–G4; guide p. 4. Output: predictions/results for A = 3 with z = 0.02, 0.12 and 0.50; balances for z = 0.12 and 0.50; and a tangent/energy explanation.
Worksheet p. 6, H1–H4. Attempt the new local-residual, applicability, phase-amount and combined-evidence cases before opening solutions. Keep your original answers and corrections.

Worksheet p. 6, I; existing Session 3 form. Output: LLE concept answer, consistency evidence, actual minutes spent and pace feedback; wait for the receipt and retain your files.
sessions.assessmentCheckpoint: Worksheet C4–C5 compares a worked local-residual example with your own calculation. In G3, independently check the balances for A = 3 at z = 0.12 and 0.50 using the actual calculated endpoints. The unseen review H1–H4 asks you to calculate a new local residual, interpret real isobaric data with missing excess enthalpy, evaluate a new candidate tie line and combine contrasting diagnostic results. Attempt these before viewing the separate solutions; do not transfer an earlier numerical answer.
sessions.planningNote: Plan approximately three hours, with fixed budgets of 115 minutes of calculation, investigation and reflection plus a 10-minute break. The video page reports the recording’s actual measured duration and its sum with those budgets. These are planning estimates, not measured student working times. Use ten work checkpoints plus a break. At slide 34, pause 3 minutes for G1 predictions before the complete Lab 04 demonstration on slide 35; then use the 25-minute pause at slide 36 to rerun G2–G4 independently. Continue when the specified output is ready rather than waiting for a timer.

sessions.title: Solid equilibria and adsorption
sessions.claim: The relevant equilibrium condition depends on the phases and vessel constraints.
sessions.outcome: Distinguish pure-solid SLE, bulk sublimation and surface adsorption.
sessions.deliverable: In Lab 10, compare inventories above and below the solid-depletion boundary at fixed T and V. Check the inventory balance and explain the resulting gas pressure.
sessions.preparation: Read the inventory example and classify bulk sublimation, adsorption and reaction. Prepare the three short questions on page 3.
sessions.guidingQuestion: What happens to gas pressure when the solid inventory runs out?
sessions.optionalPractice: Choose one extension: compare Henry and Langmuir in Lab 11, check a closed adsorption vessel, or explore pure-solid solubility and the eutectic assumptions in Lab 10. Optional paper exercises cover Henry gas solubility and dilute-solution osmosis (session appendix).

sessions.title: Chemical equilibrium and routes to K
sessions.claim: K is tied to a reaction basis, temperature and standard states.
sessions.outcome: Use extent and Gibbs driving force to establish equilibrium, then reconcile thermodynamic routes to K.
sessions.deliverable: In Lab 12, compare the supplied Gibbs-energy and H−TS routes at the reference temperature. Change pressure at fixed T and compare K with equilibrium extent. Check one balance.
sessions.preparation: Write the species amounts and feasible extent interval before calculating K. Prepare the three short questions on page 3.
sessions.guidingQuestion: Why can composition change while the equilibrium constant stays the same?
sessions.optionalPractice: Choose one extension: vary temperature with and without a heat-capacity correction, reverse the reaction, or scale its coefficients consistently.

sessions.title: Electrochemical equilibrium
sessions.claim: The Nernst potential expresses the cell reaction driving force.
sessions.outcome: Connect balanced half-reactions, activities, potential and Gibbs energy.
sessions.deliverable: In Lab 13, compare a concentration cell with the activities exchanged. Predict and explain the sign of E, then independently check deltaG=−nFE.
sessions.preparation: Balance the cell reaction and predict the potential sign before using Nernst. Prepare the three short questions on page 3.
sessions.guidingQuestion: What determines the sign of a concentration-cell potential?
sessions.optionalPractice: Choose one extension: scale the balanced reaction and electron count, examine activity corrections within the supported model, or explain why equilibrium voltage differs from voltage under load.

index.title: 01 · VLE and TP flash
index.predict: Predict whether a fixed-T mixture is liquid, vapor or two-phase before calculating.
steps: Run the default case and record T, P, z, model and phase.
Change pressure across the bubble/dew boundaries at the same T and z.
For a two-phase state, verify z=(1−β)x+βy independently.
index.check: Report units, both component balances and why a boundary calculation differs from a TP flash.
index.limit: The VLE solver excludes nonconvex liquid states. A temperature sweep needs an applicable temperature model.

case-study.title: 02 · Experimental case study
case-study.predict: Predict which parts of a published dataset most strongly constrain the model.
steps: Inspect the original observations and source notes.
Compare a model fit with the observations and residuals.
Explain how data coverage limits use beyond the measured interval.
case-study.check: Distinguish transcribed evidence, fitted parameters and model predictions.
case-study.limit: A fit to one dataset is not independent validation.

consistency.title: 03 · Consistency tests
consistency.predict: Predict whether a localized defect could pass an area test.
steps: Follow worksheet D1–D5 and E1–E2 and the Lab 03 demonstration. Predict before changing the consistent isothermal reference at 41 points.
Compare canceling errors and the localized defect at amplitude 0.25. Compare 41 with 161 points for the required resolution check, then restore the specified reference settings.
Run the modeling test once on the clean reference. Retain the area, local and modeling evidence with each method’s applicability and one limitation.
consistency.check: Give evidence from more than one diagnostic and state which assumptions each needs.
consistency.limit: The isothermal diagnostic neglects the excess-volume pressure term; its finite differences are teaching diagnostics. Herington is empirical for isobaric data; a local isobaric verdict needs independent excess-enthalpy information.

stability.title: 04 · Stability and LLE
stability.predict: Predict how a nonconvex mixing Gibbs curve changes the phase state.
steps: Predict the homogeneous-feed classification at the specified fixed model conditions, then compare the stable, metastable and unstable feed examples in worksheet F–G.
Compare each hypothetical homogeneous feed with the final equilibrium; inspect the entire Gibbs curve and globally supporting common tangent.
Use the actual coexisting compositions for an independent phase-amount balance. Explain how local curvature, global stability, phase composition and amount differ.
stability.check: Distinguish local curvature, metastability and global support.
stability.limit: A root with equal chemical potentials is only a candidate until stability is checked.

lle-fit.title: 05 · LLE fitting
lle-fit.predict: Predict whether one tie line uniquely identifies the parameters.
steps: Use the supplied example or paste supported tie-line observations with metadata.
Fit at fixed temperature and inspect both liquid compositions.
Compare parameter changes with composition error and the global stability check.
lle-fit.check: Report fit temperature, model convention, parameter bounds and a stability result.
lle-fit.limit: A fixed-T fit does not establish a temperature law or reliable extrapolation.

vlle.title: 06 · VLLE
vlle.predict: Predict whether T and P fix all three phase amounts in this binary example.
steps: Find a supported vapor–liquid–liquid state.
Inspect the phase compositions and fugacity equality.
Vary feasible phase amounts and independently close the feed balance.
vlle.check: Separate phase compositions from the feasible family of phase fractions.
vlle.limit: Three-phase amount degeneracy is physical; it is not necessarily solver failure.

adiabatic.title: 07 · Adiabatic flash
adiabatic.predict: Predict whether a pressure change can alter temperature at fixed feed enthalpy.
steps: Record feed enthalpy, pressure and the synthetic caloric definitions.
Solve the adiabatic flash and compare with a fixed-temperature calculation.
Check both material and energy residuals.
adiabatic.check: Include an energy balance with units as well as phase equilibrium.
adiabatic.limit: Caloric data are synthetic; this is not a general real-mixture enthalpy package.

vle-input.title: 08 · Your experimental VLE
vle-input.predict: Predict the effect of an incorrect Antoine pressure unit on inferred activities.
steps: Enter sources, component order, units and each exact Antoine form; verify Psat at one measured T.
Validate the table and inspect coverage before choosing endpoint assumptions.
Fit at least two supported models to the same data and compare residual patterns.
vle-input.check: Export the study and residuals; describe a region where the data do not justify a prediction.
vle-input.limit: This import/fitting lab assumes ideal vapor. Lab 09 compares vapor corrections but does not automatically refit this dataset.

virial.title: 09 · Virial vapor correction
virial.predict: Predict how zero Bij should compare with the ideal-vapor calculation.
steps: Start with zero coefficients to establish the ideal-vapor limit.
Change B12 while keeping the liquid model and standard-state convention fixed.
Compare phase results and inspect the truncation guard.
virial.check: Report coefficient units and validity range; compare the correction with plausible measurement uncertainty.
virial.limit: The guard is a teaching restriction, not a rigorous accuracy bound. PR/SRK and dense-vapor calculations are not implemented here.

solids.title: 10 · SLE and gas–solid equilibrium
solids.predict: Predict whether added solid changes equilibrium gas pressure before the solid is exhausted.
steps: Explore pure-solid solubility and the binary eutectic assumptions.
Use the gas–solid vessel example; vary total inventory through the solid-depletion boundary.
Check phase amounts and identify whether Gibbs or Helmholtz energy matches the imposed constraints.
solids.check: Name each phase, specify fixed T/P or T/V, and close the inventory balance.
solids.limit: Bulk gas–solid equilibrium is distinct from surface adsorption; no solid solution or chemical reaction is included.

adsorption.title: 11 · Adsorption
adsorption.predict: Predict which isotherms approach a finite monolayer capacity.
steps: Compare Henry, Langmuir, Freundlich and BET over their stated domains.
Use supported isotherm data or the synthetic example; compare fit residuals.
Inspect a closed-vessel balance; use isosteric heat only over common measured loading.
adsorption.check: State uptake basis, units, model domain and the distinction between fit and mechanism.
adsorption.limit: BET needs saturation pressure and a defensible window. Absolute and excess uptake are not interchangeable.

reaction.title: 12 · Chemical equilibrium
reaction.predict: Predict which routes to K remain usable when temperature changes.
steps: Write species amounts from extent, find the feasible interval and predict the sign of the Gibbs driving force.
Reconcile thermodynamic routes at the reference temperature; change pressure at fixed T and compare K, Q and extent.
As an extension, change T and compare constant-property and ΔCp routes with point-data applicability.
reaction.check: Check the reaction basis, standard states, lnQ−lnK and atom balances.
reaction.limit: The extent solver admits one neutral ideal-gas reaction. An observed Q is not automatically K.

electrochemistry.title: 13 · Electrochemistry
electrochemistry.predict: Predict the sign of the concentration-cell potential before calculating.
steps: Load the concentration cell and record both activities and reduction potentials.
Exchange the concentrations; then set them equal.
Double all reaction coefficients and electron counts; compare E, ΔG and ln K.
electrochemistry.check: Verify atom/charge balances, E=Eright−Eleft and ΔrG=−nFE.
electrochemistry.limit: Both E° values need the same reference and temperature. Junction potentials, kinetics and loaded-cell voltage are excluded.
